subject: biology
title: Punnett Squares & Ratios
welcome_lead: Today you'll predict children's traits like a geneticist — using a Punnett square to crack the 3:1 ratio.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology Genetic Inheritance — alleles, dominant/recessive, Punnett squares, 3:1 and 1:2:1 ratios.
final_note: You learned alleles, genotype vs phenotype, how to draw a Punnett square, and the classic 3:1 phenotype + 1:2:1 genotype ratios.

concepts.def: A version of a gene (e.g. B = brown, b = blue)
The trait you show (e.g. brown eyes)
Allele that shows whenever present (BIG letter)
Allele that shows only if both copies are recessive
Two different alleles for a gene (e.g. Bb)

walkthroughs.body_html:
Each gene comes in versions called alleles.

Capital letter = dominant (e.g. B). Small letter = recessive (e.g. b).

You carry two alleles: one from mum, one from dad.

Cross Bb × Bb. Put one parent across the top, the other down the side.

Fill the 4 boxes: BB, Bb, Bb, bb.

Genotype ratio = 1 BB: 2 Bb: 1 bb.

BB and Bb both show brown (B is dominant). Only bb shows blue.

So phenotype ratio = 3 brown: 1 blue. The classic 3:1!

mcqs.q: Two heterozygous brown-eyed parents cross (Bb × Bb). What is the expected phenotype ratio?
options: 1:1 brown : blue
3:1 brown : blue
1:2:1 brown : blue : green
All brown
Two dominant alleles
Two recessive alleles
One dominant, one recessive (heterozygous)
No alleles at all

mcqs.q: What does it mean for an allele to be 'dominant'?
options: It is expressed in the phenotype when at least one copy is present (in a heterozygote).
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
Each gene codes for an organ or body part as a whole.
A dominant allele is the most common allele in a population.

mcqs.q: What does a gene code for?
options: Each gene codes for an organ or body part as a whole.
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
Typically a polypeptide (protein) — through transcription to mRNA and translation by ribosomes.
A gene codes for a specific physical feature like eye colour directly.

mcqs.q: Why is the secondary immune response to a pathogen faster and stronger than the primary?
options: The body produces a different, more powerful antibody during the secondary response.
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
Memory cells generated during the primary response can rapidly proliferate and produce large amounts of specific antibody on re-exposure.
The pathogen becomes weaker after the primary exposure, so the body has an easier job.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Genotype”?
options: The trait you show (e.g. brown eyes)
Two different alleles for a gene (e.g. Bb)
Allele that shows whenever present (BIG letter)
The alleles you carry (e.g. Bb)

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Recessive”?
options: Two different alleles for a gene (e.g. Bb)
A version of a gene (e.g. B = brown, b = blue)
Allele that shows only if both copies are recessive
The alleles you carry (e.g. Bb)

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Heterozygous”?

The alleles you carry (e.g. Bb)
Allele that shows only if both copies are recessive
Two different alleles for a gene (e.g. Bb)

options: Allele that shows whenever present (BIG letter)
The trait you show (e.g. brown eyes)
Two different alleles for a gene (e.g. Bb)
A version of a gene (e.g. B = brown, b = blue)

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Phenotype”?
options: The alleles you carry (e.g. Bb)
Allele that shows only if both copies are recessive
A version of a gene (e.g. B = brown, b = blue)
The trait you show (e.g. brown eyes)

mcqs.q: In a Bb × bb cross, what percentage of offspring are expected to show the recessive phenotype (bb)?
Two brown-eyed parents who are both Bb have a blue-eyed child (bb). What is the chance their next child also has blue eyes?
options: 0 — it is impossible

mcqs.q: A characteristic only appears when an individual inherits two recessive alleles. Such an allele is described as:
options: Recessive
Dominant
Codominant
A mutation

mcqs.q: A Punnett square for Bb × bb predicts the offspring genotypes. What ratio of Bb to bb is expected?
options: All Bb

mcqs.q: Why can two parents who both show a dominant trait have a child who shows the recessive trait?
options: Both parents are heterozygous and each passed on a recessive allele.
A new dominant allele appeared in the child.
The child has only one allele for the gene.
Recessive traits cannot be inherited this way.

numericals.q: In a Bb × bb cross, what percentage of offspring are expected to show the recessive phenotype (bb)?
numericals.hint: Half the boxes will be bb, half will be Bb
